When looking at the Vinyl Record Watches I designed, that memory came into my mind. And so I took an inspiration from this old computer IBM System/360 's 9-track tape , which is a magnetic-tape data storage format. I was born in 1985, so I never saw that kind of big computer systems in my real life. So that memory always stayed in me as something that gives me classic sci-fi vibes. And I wanted to bring that into reality. A vintage computer on your wrist, how sci-fi-cool is that! The Design And so I wanted to make it like this, utilizing both the case and the dial of the Vinyl Record Watch, but with a new chapter ring and the second, minute, hour disks. The second disk and the chapter ring are in off-white color. watches.name: Cassette Tape Watch Prototype Limited
watches.description: Ok so we have a Vinyl Record Watch , what comes next? Cassette Tape of course! I tried to design within a limitation of the Cassese Tape design. This time, the idea I came up with was to use one of the gear teeth of the tape rotation system to be used as the hour indicator. And the minute is indicated by the black "tape" bits, but instead of showing exact minute, it can only roughly show you that it's closer to 0 or closer to 30 min: Yes my execution here is far from perfect. It is VERY difficult to see which hour it is as the red part is very difficult to see. (As for the minute function, I merely put the oval disks to imitate the look, which a very little legibility. So that part is at least intentional design) The "crowns" are made to look like the bottom of a hexagonal pencil. And as you may know a pencil was an important tool when the tape gets loose. Also you can see holes on the case from this angle, which can be used to hang this watch from your neck. It also comes with several different stickers: So you can stick it to the watch and have fun! <3 Dial: Interestingly, that white background thing in-between the "tape-minute-disks" is what is usually considered as a watch dial. Hands: Unique hour disks, unique oval minute disks, and unique rotating 3D "spindle"! Case: A brand new Cassette Tape case! (there was previously a prototype that didn't work, with a slightly different case shape) Movement: Two TMI quartz movements Strap: Genuine leather, the spring bar for this one is slightly curved to make it fit onto this thin watch!

Shipping estimated November 2026* American Quilt - An Adi x Ando Collaboration Commemorating America's 250th Year of Independence A quilt represents more than a pattern. It is a record of the hands, places, stories, and traditions that come together to make something whole. Inspired by the Eight-Pointed Star quilt pattern, one of America’s enduring quilt patterns —a simple geometric form built from individual pieces of fabric, each distinct on its own, yet transformed when brought together. Its beauty lies in that combination: difference becoming coherence, individual pieces becoming a larger story. The Adi x Ando collaborative dial turns the familiar motif of the Eight-Pointed Star and the Star-Spangled Banner into an expression of American identity. Red, blue, and ivory - through a Mother of Pearl dial - come together in a pattern that feels at once traditional and contemporary, while the surrounding geometry echoes the structure of a quilt block. Like a quilt itself, the dial is an American tapestry: assembled from separate elements, shaped by craft, and given meaning through their relationship to one another. The mother of pearl rendition gives it the quality of an old faded quilt that has been in use for ages. Each color variant is 25 pcs limited. Above is the silver case version. watches.name: *pre-order* Vinyl Record Automatic Watch Classic *Shipping end of 2026*
watches.description: ** latest batch now being assembled, shipping end of 2026** Do you like music? Do you like vinyl records? ARE YOU FEELING GROOVY!? If your answer is yes to any of these (or even none of these), this might be a perfect watch for you! Inspired by legendary (Panasonic) Technics SL-1200 turntable, powered by Miyota 9039 Premium automatic movement, this wrist watch is not really a piece to tell you the time (although it can do that well). Instead, it tells people around you what kind of human you are, a sophisticated music lover! How it Came to This Since the birth of the "Chillmatic" Vinyl Record Dial (now available on ModModeWatches ), this was the plan, to make a full watch with it. Then I designed the R-1 Mod Case "in secret", and presented it as just a rectangular, ordinally watch case for modders. "In secret", as in, with no intention to reveal this as the case designed for the Vinyl Record Player Automatic Watch. Because it seems there weren’t enough rectangular cases in the watch modding scene. And it’s actually easy to add/remove the chapter ring, because of the sandwich case construction. Also I made these Vinyl Record Hands . This design, in a way a bit confusing when it comes to checking time, was a result of seeing seemingly infinite numbers of “vinyl record / vinyl record player -inspired wristwatch” designs. Most of the existing products were made cheaply, not to withstand time, or, builds (modified watches) made using the “Chillmatic” Vinyl Record Dials :) And most of these watches just used normal watch hands, instead of utilizing the vinyl record / record player elements. So on above picture, it's showing about 12:37. Hour : The record label with the "A" logo is the hour hand-disk. Indicating the hour with the tip of the "A". (In reality the tip of “A” should be leaning slightly towards right though.) Minute : The "arm" (tonearm) of the vinyl record player is the minute hand. Yes it's not straight, it's not pointing the minute marker straight, but so you can interpret it in your own way (ie. the center of the head is pointing the minute, or the outermost edge of the head is pointing the minute. Second : The disc in the center is the center hand-disc. You can interpret in various ways, ie. when the texts on the disc is level is the 0 seconds. The Classic (a.k.a. RBS: Red-Black-Silver) The RBS (Red hands, Black dial, Silver case) is the most basic, standard, versatile, iconic, epic! watches.description: Ando × Luckyshroom Series V2 Luckyshroom — the Swiss-Australian designer behind the Flathead, a titanium digital watch produced in a limited edition of 100 pieces — reunites with Yu Ando, Japanese-Finnish designer and founder of AndoAndoAndo, for a second collaboration. Continuing a dialogue rooted in play, precision, and quiet subversion. Where the first series introduced a new perspective, Series V2 deepens it. Balance in Contrast This collection explores opposing forces. Light and shadow, motion and stillness, tradition and reinterpretation. Rather than altering the object, the approach is subtle. watches.name: A-2 雲: Oskar 大濤 Hellström x Ando - Limited Edition
watches.description: This is a fantastic collaboration between 書道家 Master of Japanese calligraphy, Oskar 大濤 Hellström, and AndoAndoAndo. Limited to 15 pcs. - 雲 - 雲 This character means 'cloud'. It is written in a stylized cursive form to capture the flowing movements of clouds soaring by high in the sky. Reminiscent of how time flows ever onward. The careful use of speed and ink management results in the washi paper showing through on some places on the stroke. This is called 'kasure' and creates a lighter and flowing sensation. There are many different ways to write 雲 in cursive, and this variant is inspired by my teachers writing. The strokes are on the thicker side to create a more powerful expression and the techniques used for this is probably one of the hardest techniques to learn, because it is meant to resemble having no technique. I had been practicing this style for years before I got the approval from my teacher. Oskar 大濤 Hellström Master of Japanese calligraphy The Dial The dial with 大濤's「雲」calligraphy printed onto AndoAndoAndo's Japanese washi paper dial. The Chapter Ring A new chapter ring was developed for this limited edition. It has a black raised chapter ring with recesses functioning as hour markers. The chapter ring was inspired by 借景 / "borrowed scenery" . Which is an artistic method of using something external as the element within, traditionally used in the Chinese and Japanese gardens by utilizing mountains and other scenery elements outside of the garden as a part of the garden. In the Japanese 茶道 / "the way of tea" architects, this concept is applied sometimes having a round opening or a frame, sometimes on the wall so the garden outside of the tea room would be included as a part of the room, or as a "painting" which borrowed from the real scenery. A kanji character, unlike a phonetical letter, is a word. And a word is a way to objectify an idea or a phenomenon , in order to convey its idea to other people. In this case, simplifying and making the elements / meaning of what "cloud" somewhat abstract in that process. However this way we can convey its concept, making something that is seen and felt subjectively into an objective element. Having that at the center of the dial, with this chapter ring functioning as a window or a frame, a looking glass, and it cuts out the world of Japanese calligraphy, and the character "cloud" framed onto your wrist. The Caseback The exhibition caseback features another masterful calligraphy from 大濤. 「大濤」and 「日」for 日本 / Japan, and「芬」for 芬蘭 / Finland. The Package This limited special edition comes in a leather watch pouch, with 「雲」branded on the surface. The Price and Philosophy The price of this watch is high mostly due to it having the Urushi dial, and this watch being piece-unique. And the very fact of its widespread use serves as proof of its functional beauty, reliability, practical elegance, and excellence as an industrial product, echoing the principles of the German Werkbund and the Bauhaus. And the combination of the trustworthy mass production movement, allows this watch to have the hand-crafted elements without making it too expensive. Also the cost wise, the maintenance / repair / replacement cost for the NH movement would be lower than of the Swiss. Also I would like to note that this watch was put together in Finland, by a Finnish watchsmith. watches.description: VinylPilot Watch A collaboration between Minimal Wear and AndoAndoAndo Introduction Following the success of the original Vinyl Record Watch—designed originally by Ando to address the lack of rectangular cases in the market, but you know what is also lacking? A square watch case for slimmer wrists!—the VinylPilot continues the mission of solving overlooked needs in watch design. The result is a vintage-inspired pilot watch that blends thoughtful minimalism with instrumental aviation cues. Case The VinylPilot features a 36mm × 36mm square case in black PVD stainless steel. Drawing from the rugged aesthetics of vintage cockpit instruments, the top and bezel are fully redesigned on the foundation of the original Vinyl Record case. The bezel is secured with four exposed screws for an industrial, tool-watch feel—proportioned to suit every wrist without compromise. Case Back Flipping the watch reveals a transparent sapphire case back, where the spirit of aviation comes to life. Printed on the glass is a terrain elevation map of Kitty Hawk, North Carolina—the site of the Wright brothers’ first powered flight in 1903. A radar-like graphic points precisely to the location of takeoff. As the rotor spins, it mimics the motion of an airplane propeller, reinforcing the watch’s deep aviation heritage with every movement. Dial The dial inspired by the design codes introduced in the first collaboration (Ref 22-00), while evolving its visual identity. It carries a subtle nod to California dials, reinterpreted through minimalist lens. Soft indentations create gentle depth and textured feel, while four directional lines extend outward from the center—representing orientation, navigation, and movement. The triangular 12 o’clock marker, along with the chapter ring, features arrows that points to the cardinal directions, further grounding the design in a pilot’s visual language. Hands Bold, classic sword-style hour and minute hands are filled with Super-LumiNova C3 for powerful legibility, day or night. The second hand is modeled after a radar needle—elongated and tipped with lume—sweeping gracefully across the dial with the precision of a flight instrument. ⸻ Color Options Sky Blue & Solar Flare Both of these dials are housed in the square black VinylPilot case, designed for skyward explorers. • Sky Blue features a fully lumed BGW9 dial that glows in a soft, sky blue—ideal for those drawn to altitude and clarity. • Solar Flare offers a warm, radiant tone with C3-lumed indices, evoking sunlight at cruising altitude. Together, these variations represent the dual nature of the sky—tranquil and powerful. Green Forest & Sunflower These two colorways utilize the rectangular Vinyl Record case, chosen for its unique crown guard that were designed not just to mimic the shape of a record player. But the openings in the guards allow the watch to be worn as a pendant or necklace, making it a true tool for land-dwellers, explorers, and navigators. • Green Forest features a rich, earthy green dial with a black chapter ring and hands—rooted, steady, and ready for the trail. • Sunflower contrasts with a bold, vibrant yellow dial, offering maximum legibility and warmth. Both are framed in silver-tone cases that stand apart from the black square models, signaling their distinct terrain and purpose. watches.name: AndoAndoAndo x Minimal Wear Ref.22-00 Limited Edition
watches.description: A fantastic collab with Ando and Minimal Wear, an unique, stylish, minimal, super cool GMT watch! Product Description A precision-built GMT watch with modern utility and minimal design. Every element is engineered with purpose — from the case geometry to the details on the dial — balancing legacy cues with industrial clarity. And this is the Limited Edition, which has a XX/10 serial number on the case back! ⸻ Case The case is a perfect circle, chosen for its symmetry, functionality, and symbolic continuity. • The rotating 24-hour bezel features a lumed “00” marker instead of “24” — a subtle but practical shift that aligns with how time actually resets. • The crown is low-profile and semi-recessed, maintaining clean side lines while remaining fully operable. • Laser-engraved minute markers are integrated directly into the case structure — optimizing space and eliminating the need for an outer minute track on the dial. Dial Positioned next to the date window are four engraved lines, serving as subtle indicators of discipline, persistence, commitment, and consistency — fundamentals of structured timekeeping. At 6 o’clock, dual vintage-inspired lume bars in muted green and beige reference classic lume tones from early tool watches — adding a touch of warmth to an otherwise clean dial layout. The rest of the dial follows a geometric minimalism — fine lines and hollow circles positioned with balance and clarity, with a subtle nod to the asymmetry of California-style dials. Hands Time-telling is direct and legible: • A bold arrow-shaped GMT hand • Clean, elongated hour and minute hands • A hollow circle seconds hand for continuous motion and subtle visual rhythm Each element is straightforward, architectural, and intentionally simple — built for readability, not excess. Specifications • Movement: TMI NH34 automatic GMT • Lume: Swiss BGW9 Super-LumiNova • Case Material: 316L stainless steel (*Black version PVD coated) • Case Diameter: 40mm • Lug Width: 20mm • Lug-to-Lug: 41mm • Thickness: 11mm • Crystal: Sapphire with anti-reflective coating • Bezel: 24-hour rotating bezel with lumed “00” marker • Water Resistance: 50 meters / 5 ATM • Crown: Screw-down, minimal profile • Strap Compatibility: Fits 20mm straps The Design Process *above image is slightly different from the finished product We really cared smallest details on this watch, from the bezel insert to the lug to the position of the movement inside of the case! And we are very happy to finally bring this to life. We have been working for this secretly for more than 6 months! *above image is slightly different from the finished product One of the things we decided early on the designing process is to make this watch hold the NH34 GMT movement, with a rotating bezel, while keeping the thickness of the case relatively thin. For this we decided to make the water resistance 5 ATM, knowing that people always wants higher water resistance rating, while in reality majority of them don't get into the situation that requires the water resistance rating above 5 ATM. This is a great example of having a design concept, and use reasonings to decide on the details.

watches.name: Portrait of Vsevolod Garshin 28.5mm
watches.description: Here is a 28.5mm dial I have painted using acrylic paints, coated with a paint varnish. The dial is inspired by a painting by Ilya Repin , titled " Portrait of Vsevolod Garshin " and originally painted in 1884. Ilya Repin (1844-1940) was a Russian painter born in Kharkov Governorate (current Ukraine). One of his most famous paintings was "Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan" , which was controversial, and also the very first painting to be banned in Russia. Repin bought a house in Kuokkala in 1898 (at that point Kuokkala was a part of Grand Duchy of Finland, under the Russian Empire). After the independence of Finland in 1917 though, in 1948 that part of Finland was taken by Russia, and the place was re-named to Repino, after the artist's name. Vsevolod Garshin (1855-1888), the model of the original painting, was a Russian author of short stories, who was born in Yekaterinoslav Governorate (current Ukraine). Also, he was the model of the aforementioned "Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan"'s son Ivan. Garshin had mental illness, and attempted to commit suicide (failed) but subsequently lost his life as the result of the injuries in 1888. I intend to use a part of the sale of this dial to be donated to a mental health organization or something.

watches.name: UFO Watch Prototype 36mm
watches.description: Have you watched the U.S. House of Representatives hearing of a United States Air Force (USAF) officer and former intelligence official testifying under oath about non-human spacecraft?? No? Are you a believer? Non-believer? Experiencer? Well anyway, here is the thing. This fantastically lumed and polished turbine dial , was originally found in a secret UFO watch case design. How else we could come up with such an avantgarde futuristic watch dial?? I think it was 2022 I was making this UFO full watch design. I think at that time, I was a bit tired of making practical watch designs, and I wanted to make something that is very different, fun, and unique. Also, I wanted to make something that is thinner than the NH35/36 movements. And so this UFO Watch concept was made. With the Miyota 9039 movement, and pretty much ignoring the readability, but with fun lumed elements, and a rotating bezel. I really wanted to make the UFO watch, but the cost was a real big obstacle for me. So I started to make a part of it, the dial. And luckily for me, Namoki (Namoki exclusive color already sold out!) and ModModeWatches (still available!) were interested in selling these dials in 2023. But I think now is the time to revive the old, round, strange-looking watch concept. The pre-order price is 380 EUR, and most of the cost are molding and assembly. This is because making completely new case and bezel molds are expensive. HOWEVER! If the payment was made on PayPal, and if it was sold to an EU country, my profit is minus 25.07 EUR, so it's a good deal for pre-order customers! I'm really a bad businessman! :D But at this point, it's more important for me to make the molds (which is the most expensive part) with this, rather than to make profit. - The UFO - So it's really a weird watch. Many radial lines. The dial, the case, the bezel, the crown. The case having a kind of chapter ring, but with lumed lines on each 5 minute places. The bezel also has the radial lines, and one pip that can be used in many ways. The lugs are kind of hidden, and made to look like... landing gears of a UFO? And I would imagine this case would attract a lot of dusts, and so as the so called "wrist-cheese". But this is what I call a necessary sacrifice to achieve this aesthetics. It's just... I wanted you to know that it's a design decision, instead of something that I didn't think about when designing it. - Specs - Movement: Miyota 9039 Case Diameter: 36 mm Case Body Thickness (Case top to Case Bottom excluding the crystals and the lugs): 9.58 mm Case Body Thickness (Top Crystal to Bottom Crystal): 10.07 mm Case Body Thickness (Top Crystal to Bottom Lug): 12.71 mm Lug-to-Lug: 31.45 mm Lug Width: 20 mm Water Resistance: 5 ATM Crystals (front and back): Sapphire Crystals Lume: Swiss Bracelet: Something like this flexible old-school metal strap with several endlinks for adjusting the size. - Earlier Prototypes - Prototypes were made with a 3D printer called Prusa mini+ from Prusa Research . It... kind of looks like a space-turtle?

watches.name: A-2 Auto
watches.description: It has been almost one year since the prototypes were made, but finally we will bring the A-2 Auto product edition! So, this is the follow up to the A-1 Auto, which is simply called A-2 Auto. This watch has the same movement as the A-1 Auto, TMI NH 36, and the mod-ability is also as high as the A-1. But it's a very different watch. - A-2 Auto, Symmetrical Watch - With A-2 Auto, While the basic design principle is kept the same -the crown will never hit the back of my hand-, I made it more symmetrical. It will now allow people who wear watches on the right wrist wear it as comfortably as the ones who wear it on the other wrist. Also making it symmetrical would bring a good contrast between the A-1 and the A-2. - Not Just Another A-1 - But I thought making the case symmetrical is not enough reason to justify a making of another watch. But to bring something different. Which are the minute markers, and the vertical day-date. There might be no need for markers in every minute, especially for a movement that has an accuracy of -20 ~ +40 seconds. But then again, if someone would like to count something for a few dozens of seconds, it would be useful. - Vertical Day-Date - Another difference is the vertical day-date. It is something you would only see in vintage watches, and most likely you have seen some Seiko and Citizen from the 70's. (Yes non-Japanese watch companies like Zodiac, Rado, Timex also made these too.) You don't see these recently, and I'm a bit sad about it. So here it is. The fact that the Japanese language is traditionally written vertically... is not really related to this decision, but the fact I couldn't find any vertical day-date discs as the NH3X modding part, is. - The Crown Position - Also, I have tried to fix the major problem the A-1 had... Or did I? On the A-1, the crown was so small it was difficult to pull out. Now the crown is 7 mm in diameter, so it should be easier to pull out. BUT, the crown is now situated behind of the strap, it IS LESS ACCESSIBLE! But then again, if you wear this watch on your wrist every day, how often do you need to touch the crown? So I think this position, where the crown doesn't annoy the back of hand on either wrist, is justifiable as the benefit outweighs the limiting access to the crown. *It is usually recommended not to adjust the crown while you are wearing the watch, as it might bend the crown stem. It is also true in this watch's case. - Color Variation - This time, we are bringing you several color options: Tuxedo The iconic black and white "Tuxedo", which was the most popular color variant in the A-1 Auto. This is non-limited edition. But each will have the serial number engraved. It will be something like "1st batch XXX/100" as 100 pcs of the Tuxedo variant will be produced as the first batch. Neo Tottori This time, with the collaboration with my Finnish friend and designer Joni Kallio, we have a special limited edition. It's called "Neo Tottori"! "Tottori? What is it? Is it related to Totoro?" Well my friend, Tottori city, Tottori prefecture, Japan (wikipedia) , is where I was born and raised. There is nothing sci-fi about this old small city I call my hometown. Tottori prefecture is the least populated prefecture in Japan, and more than half of the population of Tottori city is over 65 years old. Joni states: I think the idea was kind of bringing the neon lights that are commonly seen in Tokyo to Tottori. The concept of Neo Tokyo is also this futuristic version of Tokyo that’s been seen video games, anime, music etc. But so, why don't we bring more vibrance to Tottori? There you go, Neo Tottori! :D Only 50 pcs will be made of this color, and each is engraved with serial number! There is also an engraving of “YUJO” which means “friendship” in Japanese, and this comes from my first name Yu and Joni’s “Jo” combined! - Modder Friendly - One of the many things I found through the A-1 Auto, is the love and passion of the watch modding community! watches.name: AAA x 3DC: King Samurai Kanji Dial 28.5mm Pre-Order
watches.description: This dials was made in collaboration with a talented dial maker in Germany, 3dc.ing ! *Shipping estimated mid-Feb View this post on Instagram A post shared by @3dc.ing Why is it called King Samurai? The thing I hated most when seeing most of these kanji index dials, is the letters used on Eleven and Twelve o'clock. One, Two Ten Because Ten is 十, Eleven and Twelve in Japanese are "Ten one" and "Ten two", which uses two letters "十一" and "十二", and therefore destroys the dial symmetry. Samurai, a.k.a. Eleven But in Japan in certain context the Eleven could be described as Samurai, as a kanji character that describes a samurai is a combination of Ten and One, "士" (usually, or rather exclusively this happens when describing the eleventh month of the year, November, as a part of word play*). King And then I thought, what kanji would appear when Ten and Two combined, and that is King, "王". So King, and Samurai, King Samurai :D *The original word play is "西向く侍", pronounced as "nishi muku samurai". This wordplay is probably made in order to easily remember the months that has shorter than 31 days. So "ni" means 2, "shi" means 4, "mu" could mean 6, and "ku" 9. And "samurai" as I mentioned above. And all these combined, the meaning of "nishi muku samurai" becomes, "Samurai facing West"! What a cool wordplay! Why is it Pixelized? Because it's cool! :D And I also wanted to show people how interesting kanjis / Chinese characters could be. When kanji is written by hand, or in calligraphy, kanjis look very organic. But kanjis can also be so square and pixelized, and still contain meanings. Q: What size is it? A: 28.5mm diameter, with 2mm diameter hole in the middle. Q: What material is it? A: Brass! And it will patina! Q: Can I prevent patina? A: Yes but it would change the look. You can apply high gloss or matte varnish! Q: Are there dial feet? A: No. But it comes with dial stickers! Q: What's that tiny text below cannon pinion / the center? A: It's so tiny but it says "AAA" for AndoAndoAndo! (Maybe I should make it bigger if we would make a next version)

watches.name: C-1 Prototype
watches.description: The C-1 Prototype Most of the watches for children currently available on the market are cheap. To sell these watches for cheap, these are cheaply made with low quality materials, bad for environment as these don't last. But I wanted to change that. Also there are not so many small-sized watches that doesn't look like a jewelry. That is why I designed the C-1. I wanted the C-1 to be: Safe The C-1 is made with a Titanium case, which is a hypoallergenic (much less likely to cause an allergic reaction) material, instead of usual Stainless Steel (which is known to cause itch reacting with sweat on skin). Comfortable Small and thin (31.5mm diameter, 7.52mm thickness) Lightweight (Titanium is lighter than Stainless Steel) The crown is at 12 o'clock position so the crown will not hit the back of the hand Tough The Titanium case is harder, than Stainless Steel nor Plastic! The front crystal is made of scratch resistant Sapphire Crystal. The water proof rating is 10 ATM (withstands pressure equivalent to water depth of 100 meters) Lasting The particular Swiss Ronda movement used for this watch lasts 10 years with just one battery! The movement is made of metal (instead of cheap plastic parts) and repairable! Unique & Fun Each hands are in different color and texture (The hour hand is orange and matte, the minute hand is red and mirror finished, also it would be easier to remember how to read time). The number "6" on the dial has a hole, and through there you will see a different shape or color every day! Easily change the strap with the Quick-Release pins, so your child can easily change the style of the watch! Above image is my son wearing it, his wrist is 11.5 cm. Due to the limited size availability of the straps, the wrist size of 11.5cm is probably the smallest size for this watch to be worn. For the future mass production version (hopefully that would happen sometime in the near future), I will try my best to make smaller straps for this. But then again, the straps are removable, and if you have a shorter 18mm-width strap that would allow you to wear it even if you wrist is smaller than 11.5cm. Here is my wife, 15cm. And me, 16.5cm. Maybe one silicone or rubber, and another comfortable NATO. This is something I should decide with the pre-order customers. So I designed the A-2, this time with a screw-on case back, a bigger crown, higher water resistance at 10 ATM, and with paper material that doesn't produce particles. Other Ways You Can Help Please share this project! Let the people who are interested in modding, who might be interested in unique dials, know about this campaign! <3 <3 <3 Thank you so much for your time, and have a WONDERFUL DAY! -Yu

watches.name: *available at ModModeWatches* "Chillmatic" Vinyl Record Dial
watches.description: !!NOW AVAILABLE EXCLUSIVELY ON MODMODE WATCHES !! Do you like music? Do you like vinyl records? Do you like fun watch dial? ARE YOU FEELING GROOVY!? If your answer is yes to any of these (or even none of these), this might be a dial for you! The coolest mod dial of them all, the Chillmatic is here! Dimension: 28.5 mm Dial legs: for both 3 O'clock dial position and 3.8 O'clock position for NH35/36/37/38/39 We tried to design the grooves, the texture, and the center part of the vinyl record on a watch dial! With a help of a Finnish DJ we made it as groovy as it is, with cool texts as reference to the wonderful world of vinyl records! Example Builds Yep, it looks quite groovy on an A-1 Mod Case ! Above are cool builds by @esinemotiivi ! Here is a gorgeous build by Henning Heisenberg ! Behold, the Vinyl Record Dial , and the Record Player Exhibition Case ! This tiny little cute vinyl record disk and a vinyl record player is just so much fun! No you cannot play music with it, but it can be on your desk, in your office, or your house, to cheer up your life like music! <3 The Viny Record Dial is made of copper. The Record Player Exhibition Case is made of Zinc Alloy, glass top, and magnets. Yes, the upper case (the right one in above picture) attaches on the case base (the left one, with "A" logo) with magnets. So you can take out and swap the Vinyl Record Dial if you wish! Is it 1/12 Scale? That is a great question! A life-size vinyl record album is traditionally 12" (30.48cm), and 1/12 of that would be 2.54 cm. This Vinyl Record disk is 2.85 cm, so not exactly, but not too far from 1/12. A rare footage of two Sylvanian Penguins dancing in their natural habitat. They party hard. So yes, it would also be a pretty good decoration for your 1/12 miniatures! The Design I designed it on Fusion 360, and then, I have spent my saving to prototype. Because... I thought it would be fun, and what is life without fun and music? Two magnets holds the top part to the bottom part. The top part has a mineral glass, so the dial is protected from the dust. A watch dial is usually made of copper, so the dial would not be magnetized. Sadly it's not designed to stand on its own sideways (notice that there is a glass cuboid behind of it), and there is a reason for it. It's because I designed the bottom part to be modular. Not sure when that can be done, but maybe in a near future? The top part is 35 mm x 43 mm, the bottom part is about 34 x 34 mm. The total thickness is 9 mm. The vinyl record dimension is 28.5mm.

watches.name: *AVAILABLE AT ModMode* 6 Petal Sakura Dial for NH36 & Miyota 9039
watches.description: PLEASE BUY IT ON MOD MODE WATCHES! <3 Please not that some images on this page are of previous prototypes, and below changes will occur for the product edition: From the prototype (pictured above), I have made several improvements on the 6-Petal Sakura Mother-of-Pearl dial: 1. The petal directions will be changed to above images (top petal heading upwards is more traditional Japanese style Sakura pattern). 2. The logo will also moved to the 6 o'clock positon. 3. The dial will be outlined with gold / silver. This is due to the fact that the mother of pearl is very thin, and it would easily crack from the edge as seen in below image: Having outline would prevent it. 4. The previous prototype had NH36 3 o'clock and 3.8 o'clock legs, but the product edition will have NH36 3 o'clock and Miyota 9039 3 o'clock legs. 5. The previous version of the silver prototype had the "A" logo in white, the product edition will have it in silver color. SPECS! - Dial diameter: 28.5 mm - Dial thickness: 0.42 mm - legs compatible for NH 36 and Miyota 9039, both 3 o'clock crown position (You have to cut the unnecessary ones) (above is also prototype image) Yes, usually a sakura / cherry blossom flower has only 5 petals. I know. But a watch dial is usually divided into 12, and so 6 petals fits better for a watch. There is also a cool story I can tell about a 6 petaled sakura that really exists. The Space Sakura (宇宙桜, read as そらざくら / Sora-zakura) is a name that is used for cherry blossom trees that grew out of the seeds that went into to space on the Space Shuttle Endeavour OV-105 in 2008, and and stayed at the ISS 's Japanese Experiment Module "Kibō" (meaning "hope") for 8 months. There were 14 different types of blossoms from 14 different locations in Japan, but the one in particular, the one came from a very old cherry blossom tree (Cerasus itosakura) in Yamanashi prefecture's Jissou temple. This cherry blossom tree is the very first natural monument designated by Japan during the Taishō era (1912 to 1926), and said to be 2000 years old. Its name is 山高神代桜 (Yamadaka Jindai-zakura), and its descendant that traveled to space is planted in the same temple is named 宇宙神代桜 (Uchuu Jindai-zakura), adding the 宇宙 (Uchuu / space). That's a cool story right? Unfortunately though, the word Space Sakura (or more specifically, the Japanese word "宇宙桜") is a registered trademark. Although, technically, it seems the trade registration doesn't seem to cover watches, instead, other products, such as clothing products, drinks, and events. So I guess I have no problem selling this dial as Space Sakura Dial, but I would not want to cause any trouble with the trade mark owners, so now I'm asking a related party. *Please note that due to the natural Mother-of-Pearl, each dial has different pattern, which you cannot choose!*

And of course these will be serial numbered! The serial numbers will be engraved on the stainless steel part outside of the case back crystal. Prototypes will be made in approximately 30 to 40 days from the prototype order. - A-2 Auto, Symmetrical Watch - With A-2 Auto, While the basic design principle is kept the same -the crown will never hit the back of my hand-, I made it more symmetrical. Also making it symmetrical would bring a good contrast between the A-1 and the A-2. - Not Just Another A-1 - *The "A" logo will be white in the light, and lumed* But I thought making the case symmetrical is not enough reason to justify a making of another watch. But to bring something different. Which are the minute markers, and the vertical day-date. There might be no need for markers in every minute, especially for a movement that has an accuracy of -20 ~ +40 seconds. But then again, if someone would like to count something for a few dozens of seconds, it would be useful. - Vertical Day-Date - Another difference is the vertical day-date. It is something you would only see in vintage watches, and most likely you have seen some Seiko and Citizen from the 70's. watches.description: This is a prototype dial I made for the Miyota 9039 movement. Originally this dial was designed as a part of a full watch, but later I wanted to bring more people to the Miyota 9039 modding. By the time I decided to make the dial more versatile size for modding (a.k.a. 28.5mm diameter), I already started making a prototype dial for 26 mm diameter, based on the early version of the Miyota 9039 full watch idea. So here it is. These have 2 legs made to fit onto the Miyota 9039 movement. Swiss made lume is used on the bottom layer, and the top layer is mirror polished metal. Yes it's quite handy as a mirror as well. As this was originally intended as a part of a full watch, the prototype dials are sterile. In the next prototype, I will be putting the "A" logo on the dial, so if you are a fan of sterile dials, this would be the only opportunity to get this dial design in sterile. There are only 5 of these (plus 1 color variant) in existence. So it's pretty rare! I understand at the moment there are not so many mod parts options such as chapter rings, watch cases etc, hands, but at least here is your chance to get an unique dial! If you would like to use it for the SII NHXX movements, there is nothing stopping you from doing that. I actually cut the dial legs and taped it on the NH36 movement holder. I'm sure you can do it much better than I did here, by using some kind of extra dial behind of it, or using a chapter ring on top of it etc.

I thought people would feel more comfortable backing on a campaign that is on a known crowdfunding platform, rather than a small microbrand's website. But if Indiegogo is failing it, then it would be better to just have a pre-order on my website. (But if you are more comfortable pre-ordering the dial on Indiegogo, here is the link! ) Short Summary Hello, my name is Yu Ando, a designer and owner of AndoAndoAndo. I'm originally from Japan, studied design in Japan, but now living with my family in Helsinki, Finland. I have previously made A-1 Automatic watch , and then absolutely blasted by the love, passion and enthusiasm of watch modding community! Then made A-1 Mod Cases , with the support from the community. And here it is, another design, this time brand new, for any NH36 rocking modders to enjoy! DDID, Day-Date Integrated Dial! So here it is, the DDID (Not to be confused with: Describe, Determine, Implicate and Direct / Decontamination and Decommissioning Integrated Demonstration / Dispensable Drug Identifier). I was always annoyed that the window for the day/date discs having different shape to the indexes, making the day/date opening an element that destroys the symmetry. So I made the indexes the same shape as the window! Now, if you know me, you know that I am bad with colors, so naturally the colors is limited to black and white. But then I was wondering for a why that why there are only a handful of black lumes around ( ModModeWatches , and NamokiMOD sells dials with black lume by the way). And of course the reason is that black color absorbs photons, so the lume is not as bright = not as useful. But I wanted to have some playfulness in this dial. So I added the black lume in the index, to separate the index into two, just like the day and date disks are separated. The lume we use is all Swiss made BGW9, including the black part. So the black (under the lighting) lume is basically a mixture of BGW9 and black paint. But wait a minute, white index outer would match a white date disk, but you would need a black day disk? Yes you would! After the manufacturing, this dial will be sold exclusively on ModModeWatches (which currently sells my A-1 Mod Cases !), and you know what? ModModeWatches sells exactly that ! Seemingly empty dial, but if you look closely to above 6 O'clock index, you will see that the AndoAndoAndo logo is subtly put there on the glossy dial. This prototype only has 2 legs on the back, but the product edition will have 4 legs, so it can be easily attached into a SKX case (with crown position around 4 O'clock), or more traditional 3 O'clock crown position case. You just have to cut the extra legs with a nipper ( Lucius Atelier kindly has an article about it). watches.name: Watch Stand MIF: Hand Made in Finland, with Finnish Materials
watches.description: Yes, it is not cheap. But it is ethical, hand made, in Finland, with Finnish materials. If you would prefer an affordable watch stand, please check our " Very Affordable Watch Stand for Every Watch Fan! " -Versatile Watch Stand- This watch stand is designed to hold rather small watch comfortably. However, it is also versatile, for example... You can hold a pocket watch: A metal bracelet watch: Or two! And there is a small space to hold some other small object, such as cuff links: -Made with Northern Finnish Birch- Did you know that many mass manufactured wooden products use so called "fast grown wood"? These are grown fast, and cut as soon as it grows enough to be sold. These are indeed cheap and often come from environmentally unethical conditions. The wood we used for this project are grown slowly, natural conditions, in Northern Finland. The harsh nature of Northern Finland made these birches strong, and beautiful. -Hand Made in Finland- These stands are not mass manufactured with automated machines. Every single piece is hand cut, hand assembled, hand varnished in Western Finland, by a family owned wood workshop. -The Price- You might consider that this is expensive for a watch stand. Yes indeed a wooden watch stand using unethical materials, fast growing trees, and mass produced, would be much more affordable. But AndoAndoAndo would like to move the manufacturing to more local, small quantity, and hand made in the future, and this product is one of the first steps for us to head to that direction. Again, it is not cheap. But it is ethical, and hand made, in Finland, with Finnish materials. And I believe, no matter how small the number is, there are people who would resonate with our philosophy, who think that this is worth paying the money for. Still not convinced? How about this? :D YES THIS WATCH STAND CAN HOLD AS MANY AS 6 WATCHES!!! >:D I'm sure if you a master of a object-stacking game, you can put more! So very much high cost performance, when considering the price-per-the-number-of-watch-that-can-be-on-the-watch-stand, it could compete with much more affordable watch stand for sure.
